relationship: Fixed-width registers connect number representations, arithmetic and bit operations to the values they encode, the results they produce and the information lost through overflow or shifts.

learnerLoop.action: Choose a curriculum and question range, reason from the register, and enter or select an answer.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The generated task applies a representation or operation permitted by the selected curriculum; the learner’s answer is checked against that task.
learnerLoop.evidence: Register bits, place values, operation displays, answer feedback and worked explanations connect the result to its representation and bit width.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Use the evidence to correct the reasoning, compare representations or operations, or practise another task within the selected curriculum.

invariants: Bit patterns, numeric interpretations and worked answers agree with the stated representation and register width.
Unsigned overflow, signed overflow and bits lost or recirculated in a shift remain distinguishable.
Generated tasks belong to the selected curriculum; showing hints or changing the question range does not introduce AS-only content into IGCSE.
safeAdaptations: Vary values, contexts, visual representations and working support while preserving the mathematical meaning of the register and operations.
Reorganise practice or add explanations within the documented curriculum features; extend curricular content only when explicitly requested.
nonGoals: Floating-point representation and processor execution are outside this integer-register practice lab.
A harder question does not by itself justify introducing a feature from another curriculum.

integer-conversions.description: Convert between positive denary and fixed-width binary integers.

unsigned-arithmetic.description: Add positive binary integers and identify fixed-width overflow.

logical-shifts.description: Apply logical shifts and relate discarded bits to the resulting unsigned value.

twos-complement.description: Represent and negate signed integers using two’s complement.

ones-complement.description: Convert signed integers between denary, one’s complement and two’s complement.

bcd-conversions.description: Encode and decode individual decimal digits using Binary Coded Decimal.

storage-prefixes.description: Distinguish decimal and binary magnitude prefixes when converting storage quantities.

signed-arithmetic.description: Add and subtract signed binary integers and detect signed overflow.

arithmetic-shifts.description: Apply arithmetic shifts to signed registers, preserving or interpreting the sign.

cyclic-shifts.description: Rotate bits through a fixed-width register.

bitwise-operations.description: Apply AND, OR and XOR masks and use masks to set or test a selected bit.

hexadecimal-conversions.description: Convert integers between denary, binary and hexadecimal.

cambridge-9618-as.label: Cambridge International AS Level Computer Science 9618

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Incomplete and incorrect submission feedback; successful answers additionally reveal the worked solution.
completion.visibility: checkAnswer() uses #feedback for incomplete, wrong and correct submissions; a worked solution requires correctness.

settings.description: Existing profile/range switches and place-value support.
settings.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

answer-check.description: Mutually exclusive result forms and explicit answer checking.
answer-check.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

new-question.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

given-registers.description: The generated question supplies scalar values, one or more register rows, operation operands, shifts or masks.
given-registers.domain: Positive/signed integer values and fixed-width bit strings; storage magnitudes when selected.
given-registers.source: Generated from the selected profile and range.
given-registers.output: Prompt, register bits and representation labels are immediately visible; place-value help depends on help state.

requested-result.description: One requested result per question: binary register, denary integer, hexadecimal string or yes/no decision.
requested-result.domain: Width/representation constrained by the generated question; yes/no for decision questions.
requested-result.source: Learner produces the requested conversion, operation result or decision.
requested-result.output: Checking compares the assembled/normalised answer with the generated expected value; correct feedback reveals the worked explanation.

modes.curriculum: Existing verified contract.curriculum profiles control the IGCSE/AS question pools. These are preserved; this implementation map adds no alignment.
modes.range: [data-range] chooses Binary, Binary + Hex or Full range within the selected profile. Full range is an integer-operation range, not floating-point support.
modes.support: #helpButton previews or pins place-value help. There is no None/Some/All Working setting in this implementation.

dependencies: Profile and range selection generate a permitted question before answer controls are built.
Binary digit inputs are separate physical bit slots composing ONE register answer; the denary/hex field or yes/no pair is an alternative input form, not additional unknowns.
Check answer requires a complete submission. New question changes the task; help does not change the permitted curriculum pool.
implementation.completion: checkAnswer() marks state.correct only when readAnswer().value equals question.answer.value. A worked solution appears in #feedback; there is no modal completion gate.
limitations: The Full range label must not be read as support for floating-point questions; the contract explicitly excludes them.
